area: Adding a new native employee skill (SkillData) from a mod — Big Ambitions Build 3672
findings:
## 1. The full SkillData type

Decompiled at `decomp/BigAmbitions.Characters/BigAmbitions.Characters.decompiled.cs:603-641` (namespace `BigAmbitions.Characters.Skills`, assembly `BigAmbitions.Characters`):

```
[CreateAssetMenu(menuName = "BigAmbitions/SkillData")]
public class SkillData : TaggedScriptableObject
{
    public string skillName;                       // dict key; also the localization key used verbatim (skill.name.GetLocalization())
    public float  baseHourlyWage;                  // value type
    public float  trainingCostMultiplier = 1f;     // value type, field initializer = 1f
    [AutocompleteDropdown("Skills")]
    public string secondarySkill;                  // string; "" / null means "no secondary skill"
    [MinMaxSlider(1,100)]
    public Vector2Int secondarySkillRange = new Vector2Int(5, 20);   // value type, initializer (5,20)
    public Sprite   icon28;                         // UnityEngine.Object ref — CANNOT be `new`ed
    public Gradient associatedColorGradient;        // plain managed class — `new Gradient()` is legal
    public List<string> possibleDealbreakers;       // ref, may be null
}
```

`Skill` (the per-employee instance struct, same file `:605-616`): `public string name; public float value; int GetRoundedValue()`. Employees hold `characterData.skills : List<Skill>`; `GetPrimarySkill()` = `skills.First().name`.

Base `TaggedScriptableObject` lives in assembly `BigAmbitions.Tags` and is NOT in this decomp. From usage: it exposes `public void BuildTagCache()` (called by `AddressableLoader.cs:95` for every loaded tagged SO, and by `BusinessTypeHelper.RegisterModBusinessType` `Helpers/BusinessTypeHelper.cs:69`) and `bool HasTag(int)` + `bool HasTag(string)` overloads. Skill tags referenced in code: `TagRef.Skilltag.hashoursperweekdemand`, `TagRef.Skilltag.forcefulltime`, `TagRef.Skilltag.canhavejobdemands` (`TagRef.Skilltag.*` are `int` constants; `TagRef` is also in `BigAmbitions.Tags`, not decompiled).

Value types (safe to set blind): `skillName, baseHourlyWage, trainingCostMultiplier, secondarySkill, secondarySkillRange`, plus `associatedColorGradient` (`new Gradient()`), `possibleDealbreakers` (`new List<string>()`). Unity-object ref that cannot be created blind: `icon28` (Sprite) — must come from an AssetBundle, or `Sprite.Create()` off a runtime `Texture2D`, or be left null.

## 2. How SkillHelper stores skills

`decomp/.../BigAmbitions.Characters.decompiled.cs:642-670`:

```
public static class SkillHelper
{
    public const string AddressableLabel = "Skills";
    private static readonly Dictionary<string, SkillData> Skills = new Dictionary<string, SkillData>();
    public static IEnumerable<string> AllSkillNames => Skills.Keys;
    public static void OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData> skillData) {
        Skills.Clear();
        Skills.EnsureCapacity(skillData.Count);
        foreach (SkillData s in skillData) Skills.Add(s.skillName, s);
    }
    public static SkillData GetData(string skillName) => Skills.GetValueOrDefault(skillName);
    public static SkillData GetData(Skill skill)      => Skills.GetValueOrDefault(skill.name);
}
```

- Dictionary type `Dictionary<string, SkillData>`, key = `SkillData.skillName` (the field, not the asset name).
- `Skills` is **private static readonly** — a mod cannot do `SkillHelper.Skills[name] = data` directly. It must reflect the field: `typeof(SkillHelper).GetField("Skills", BindingFlags.NonPublic|BindingFlags.Static)`. The dict object is `readonly` and is only ever `.Clear()`/`.Add()`ed — never reassigned — so a mod can grab that reference **once** and keep re-adding to it.
- `OnSkillDataLoaded` **REPLACES** (`Skills.Clear()` first) and does **not** preserve any mod collection. Contrast `Helpers/BusinessTypeHelper.cs:23-50` `OnBusinessTypesLoaded`, which re-adds a separate `ModBusinessTypes` dict after every reload — skills have no such mechanism.
- `GetData` returns **null** for an unknown skill (never throws). The crashes come from unguarded dereferences of that null at the call sites (section 5).
- There is **no public skill-registration API**. `BAModAPI.ModdingAPI` (`decomp/BigAmbitions/BAModAPI/ModdingAPI.cs`) exposes only `RegisterModBusinessType` / `RegisterModVehicleType` (+ Unregister). No `RegisterModSkill`.

## 3. When the skill list (re)loads

Registration point: `AddressableLoader.RegisterAll()` → `Register<SkillData>("Skills", SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded)` at `decomp/BigAmbitions/BigAmbitions.SaveSystem/AddressableLoader.cs:170`. `Register<T>` (`:76-101`) does `Addressables.LoadAssetsAsync<T>(label)`, and for each `TaggedScriptableObject` result calls `.BuildTagCache()` (`:93-95`) before invoking the callback.

`AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll()` (which runs `RegisterAll` + force-loads, wiping & repopulating `Skills`) is called from **exactly two places**, both in `SaveGameManager.cs`:
- `:339` — `TryPrepareLoad` (loading an existing save)
- `:466` — new-game creation

It is **NOT** re-run on city↔main-menu transitions, subway travel, or the blueprint creator (`MainMenuController.cs:107` uses `RegisterMainMenu()` and `RegisterBlueprintCreator()`, neither of which registers `"Skills"`). So `Skills` is repopulated once per save-load / new-game, and mod entries added afterward survive until the next save-load.

Ordering on a save load (`SaveGameManager.LoadAsync` → `TryPrepareLoad` → `CompleteLoad` → `LoadScene.LoadGame` → `UI.Load/LoadingScreen.cs:90-123`):
1. `GlobalEvents.Init()` (resets one-shot `_onGameLoaded`)
2. `AddressableLoader.RegisterAndLoadAll()` — **`Skills` populated here**
3. deserialize save, compat fixes
4. loading screen: unload MainMenu mod scope → load city scenes → `ModLifecycleLoader.LoadScopeAsync(ModActivationScope.City)` — **runs `[ModEntryOnCityLoad]` `OnLoadAsync`, awaited** (`LoadingScreen.cs:111`)
5. `GlobalEvents.InvokeOnGameLoaded()` (`LoadingScreen.cs:123`)

Hooks a mod can attach a re-inject to, all firing **after** step 2:
- `[BAModAPI.ModEntryOnCityLoad]` on a class implementing `BAModAPI.IModBigAmbitions` (or extending `ModBigAmbitionsBase`); its `Task OnLoadAsync(ModContext)` runs every time the City scope loads and is awaited inside the loading screen, so it completes before gameplay. Scope→attribute map: `decomp/ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:17-24`. Lifecycle: `ModLifecycleLoader.cs:92-129`.
- `GlobalEvents.RegisterOnGameLoadedCallback(Action)` (`decomp/BigAmbitions/GlobalEvents.cs:117-127`) — one-shot per load; if already fired it invokes immediately; re-armed by `GlobalEvents.Init()` each load. Not a public `Action` field.
- Harmony Postfix on `SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData>)` — fires synchronously the instant the game repopulates, i.e. strictly before any consumer. This is the cleanest primary hook.

Recommended: Harmony-postfix `OnSkillDataLoaded` as primary + `[ModEntryOnCityLoad].OnLoadAsync` as backstop, both calling one idempotent `EnsureSkillInjected()` that writes into the cached `Skills` dict reference.

## 4. Runtime construction vs asset bundle

`ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>()` works from the mod DLL (it references `BigAmbitions.Characters`). The managed ctor runs, so `trainingCostMultiplier` and `secondarySkillRange` initializers apply. All of SkillData's own fields are **public**, so no reflection is needed to populate it.

Minimum viable, no-bundle SkillData that will not NPE:
```
var sd = ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>();
sd.skillName             = "yourmod:skill_storemanager";
sd.name                  = sd.skillName;            // ScriptableObject.name
sd.baseHourlyWage        = 30f;
sd.trainingCostMultiplier= 1f;
sd.secondarySkill        = string.Empty;            // MUST be empty (IsNullOrEmpty short-circuits secondarySkillRange reads)
sd.associatedColorGradient = new Gradient();        // MUST be non-null — ScheduleHelper.GetEmployeeColor calls .Evaluate() unconditionally
sd.possibleDealbreakers  = new List<string>();
// sd.icon28 left null — only one cosmetic consumer (see 5.14)
sd.BuildTagCache();                                 // MUST call — HasTag() reads a tag cache built here
```
`icon28` is the only field that genuinely needs an AssetBundle (or `Sprite.Create` off a `Texture2D` loaded from mod files). A bundle-shipped `SkillData` .asset authored in the Unity editor (referencing `BigAmbitions.Characters`) is the robust path — it gets a real icon, a real gradient, and real serialized tags. Mods load bundles via `BAModAPI.Services.AssetService`: declare `RelativeAssetBundlePaths` on the mod class, then `AssetService.GetBundle(modId, bundleKey).LoadAsset<SkillData>(name)` or `AssetService.FindAssetInAnyBundleByFileName<SkillData>("MyStoreManagerSkill")` (`decomp/BigAmbitions.ModAPI/BigAmbitions.ModAPI.decompiled.cs:1051`, `:786`). After loading a bundle asset still call `BuildTagCache()` (mirrors `AddressableLoader.cs:95`).

Open risk: whether the serialized tag field on `TaggedScriptableObject` can be set at runtime (type not in decomp). If it can't, `HasTag(...)` returns false for everything on the fallback instance — which is a SAFE default for the new roles (no forced full-time, no job demands, no hours-per-week schedule requirement) as long as `BuildTagCache()` tolerates a tagless instance. Authoring tags in a bundle .asset sidesteps this entirely.

## 5. The Harmony guard + every unguarded call site

Target signatures (both in `public static class SkillHelper`, assembly `BigAmbitions.Characters`):
- `public static SkillData GetData(string skillName)`
- `public static SkillData GetData(Skill skill)`

Guard = Harmony **Postfix** on both (Prefix also works but Postfix lets the real dictionary win and only fills a genuine miss):
```
static void Postfix(ref SkillData __result, string skillName) {
    if (__result == null && ModSkills.TryGetValue(skillName, out var sd)) __result = sd;
}
// second overload: parameter (ref SkillData __result, Skill skill) -> use skill.name
```
The guard is defense-in-depth; the injection into `Skills` (section 3) is the real fix. `ModSkills` should hand back the same fully-populated SkillData used for injection.

Fields the fallback/injected SkillData must have valid, derived from the unguarded call sites below: `skillName`, `baseHourlyWage`, `trainingCostMultiplier`, `secondarySkill` (empty), `secondarySkillRange` (only if secondarySkill set), `associatedColorGradient` (non-null), `HasTag` must not throw (`BuildTagCache()` called), `possibleDealbreakers` (non-null preferred), `icon28` (null tolerated).

Unguarded `SkillHelper.GetData(...)` dereferences (NPE when the skill is missing) — file:line:

Already-guarded (safe) call sites — no patch needed, but note the semantics:
- `Buildings.Office.Headquarters/HeadhunterHelper.cs:100-104` — `if (data == null || data.possibleDealbreakers == null ...) return Array.Empty(...)`.
- `UI.Smartphone.Apps.MyEmployees/CandidateFilterController.cs:14` and `EmployeeFilterController.cs:14` — `!string.IsNullOrEmpty(skill) && !(SkillHelper.GetData(skill) == null)`.
- `Entities/EmployeeInstance.cs:230` and `:235` — `characterData.skills.Select(x => SkillHelper.GetData(x.name)).Any(x => x?.HasTag(tag) ?? true)`. Null-safe against a crash, but **semantically wrong for a mod**: a missing skill makes `HasAnySkillWithTag(...)` return `true`. Fix by injection, not a guard.

## 6. enums.txt / ModEnumDefinitions — skills are pure-string

Skills are **never** looked up by enum or hash anywhere. `SkillHelper.Skills` is `Dictionary<string, SkillData>` keyed by string; `decomp/BigAmbitions.old/BigAmbitions.SaveSystem.Legacy/SkillLegacyMap.cs:11-13` enumerates ~30 string fields that carry skill names (`Skill.name`, `SkillData.skillName`, `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills`, `EmployeePreset.skill`, `Headhunter.skillRecruiting`, `RecruitmentSettings.selectedSkill`, etc.) — all `string`.

`ModEnumDefinitions` (`decomp/ModsInternal/BigAmbitions.ModsInternal/ModEnumDefinitions.cs`) + `enums.txt` + `BAModAPI.ModEnumHash.GetSafeHash` (SHA256 → first 4 bytes as int, bumped past 0-2000; `decomp/BigAmbitions.ModAPI/BigAmbitions.ModAPI.decompiled.cs:663-683`) is a general facility for mods to inject **values into existing C# enums** (`AppName`, `NotificationType`, `CharacterEmojiName`, …) declared as `Namespace.Type.NewValue` lines in `<modfolder>/enums.txt`, resolved at discovery time (`ModDiscoveryRegistry.cs:453` `TryDefineModEnums`). It has nothing to do with skills and should not be used for them.

## 7. Adjacent injections required for the roles to be hireable (not "the skill" itself, but blocking)

- Recruitment Agency dialog dropdown = `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills ∩ RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills` (`UI.Dialog/RecruitmentSettings.cs:63` and `:100`). To hire the new role "where the Purchasing Agent is hired" the mod must also add the skill name to (a) the relevant HQ/office `BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills` (via reflection or a Harmony postfix on `BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded`) and (b) the agency building's `RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills`.
- The Headhunter HQ tab lists `SkillHelper.AllSkillNames` minus `HeadhunterHelper.skillsToSkipWhenRecruiting` (`HeadhuntersRecruitingTab.cs:371-377`) — an injected skill auto-appears there, so add it to `skillsToSkipWhenRecruiting` if it should NOT be headhuntable.
- `Helpers/RecruitmentHelper.cs:43-50` `GenerateCandidate` switches on skillName to pick an `EmployeeInstance` subclass (`LogisticsManager`/`HRManager`/`Headhunter`/`PricingManager`, else base `EmployeeInstance`). A new skill falls through to base `EmployeeInstance` — fine functionally; a dedicated subclass needs a Harmony patch on that switch.

feasibility: Native, but needs Harmony + reflection (no asset bundle strictly required). (1) Build the SkillData: ScriptableObject.CreateInstance<SkillData>() at runtime with public field-set + BuildTagCache(), leaving icon28 null; OR ship a real .asset in an AssetBundle for icon/gradient/tags. (2) Inject: reflect `SkillHelper.Skills` (private static readonly Dictionary<string,SkillData>) once, cache the reference, and re-add the entry from BOTH a Harmony Postfix on SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded(IList<SkillData>) AND a [ModEntryOnCityLoad].OnLoadAsync backstop (skills are wiped/reloaded only on save-load & new-game, via SaveGameManager.cs:339/466). (3) Defense-in-depth Harmony Postfix on both SkillHelper.GetData(string) and SkillHelper.GetData(Skill) returning the mod SkillData when __result==null. (4) Adjacent, also required for hireability: inject the skill name into the HQ BusinessType.employeePrimarySkills and the agency's RecruitmentAgencySettings.availableEmployeeSkills. Fragility is real (private field reflection, undecompiled TaggedScriptableObject tag internals, ~18 unguarded call sites) but every failure mode has a guard. Class.method targets: SkillHelper.OnSkillDataLoaded, SkillHelper.GetData, BusinessTypeHelper.OnBusinessTypesLoaded (optional), RecruitmentHelper.GenerateCandidate (optional, for a dedicated EmployeeInstance subclass).
